The local-boundedness inequality itself is sound, but the selected docstring transposes the actual coefficient matrix. This corrects my earlier acceptance: I had relied on the prose expansion of the energy form rather than its defining flipped bilinear map. In EnergyForm/Basic.lean86–104, energyIntegrand A 0 0 U V = matrixBilinearForm A V.gradient U.gradient; Ellipticity/Basic.lean160 identifies this as (∇v)ᵀA∇u. Consequently the hypothesis is −∂ᵢ(aᵢⱼ∂ⱼu)≤0, whereas the selected docstring at Regularity/LocalBoundedness/Basic.lean959 states −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ∂ᵢu)≤0. No symmetry assumption identifies the two. On Ω=(−1/2,1/2)², A(x,y)=[[1,x],[0,1]] is bounded and uniformly elliptic, and u=−y gives actual −div(A∇u)=1 while the documented transposed expression is0. Thus the documented weak-subsolution condition does not describe the formal hypothesis. This is a mathematical calculation, not a compiled fixture. The docstring should use the actual matrix orientation. Pinned definition: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/EnergyForm/Basic.lean#L86 ; matrix convention: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Ellipticity/Basic.lean#L160 ; selected doc: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Regularity/LocalBoundedness/Basic.lean#L959 .

UniformlyEllipticOn includes0<λ≤Λ and a bound on the whole bilinear form, not merely its symmetric quadratic part. Together with coefficient measurability and H¹ integrability these make the energy integral meaningful. The ball has positive radius, finite Haar measure and lies in Ω. The truncated square is integrable there even when Ω has infinite measure; the proof restricts to that ball before using constants. The bound's constant is chosen before Ω,a,u,k,x₀,R and depends on the stated Haar normalization as well as ellipticity and dimension.

The inspected finite-measure Sobolev estimate supplies an exponent above2 in dimensions1 and2 as well as higher dimensions. Caccioppoli for positive truncations and superlinear iteration produce exactly R^(−n/2), without falsely applying the high-dimensional critical exponent to n=2. Applying the result to u and−u yields the two-sided solution bound. These three source checks pass. This is the local-boundedness part of [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/PDE/README.md#L334) E23, which separately requests Hölder continuity and Harnack. No separately tagged concrete Check accompanies this estimate. The source's De Giorgi/Han–Lin references are locators, not independently read full texts.

I read the rendered signature, docstring and definition value where applicable, compared the pinned source, and checked the prior record, including the acceptance withdrawn by this correction. Object, conventions, edges, junk values, nonvacuity, choices, generality and naming were assessed. Verification uses source inspection and the pinned sorry-free extraction, without a successful fresh Lean build.

Correction after checking the defining flipped bilinear form: my earlier acceptance incorrectly endorsed the docstring coefficient order. Replaced by problem review 6f0206a7d2ceea3b. The formal inequality remains sound; the docstring identifies its weak PDE with the transposed matrix. Existing test records remain valid.
